q:
Captured response to an unauthenticated GET https://api.shop-lab.example/actuator/env :
HTTP/1.1 200
content-type: application/vnd.spring-boot.actuator.v3+json

{"activeProfiles":["prod"],"propertySources":[{"name":"systemEnvironment","properties":{"DB_PASSWORD":{"value":"s3cr3t-prod"},"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID":{"value":"AKIAEXAMPLE7Q"}}}]}
Which defect class is this?

choices.A: Exposed Spring Boot actuator env (unauthenticated secret disclosure)

q: GET https://app.shop-lab.example/api/admin/users returns 200, content-type text/html, 1873 bytes, body starts <!doctype html><html><head><script src="/static/main.4f1c.js">. GET https://app.shop-lab.example/gnoc-nonsense-91827 also returns 200, text/html, 1873 bytes, identical body. What is this?

choices.C: SPA soft-200 false positive: the app shell is served for every path

q: GET https://www.hotel-lab.example/api/pwa/updateHotelCall?url=http://bff-internal.corp-lab.example/ping returns 200 {"request_id":"7f2a...","service":"bff-internal","status":"UP"}. The host bff-internal.corp-lab.example resolves only to 10.12.4.8 and is unreachable from the internet. The same call with url=https://bff-internal.corp-lab.example/ping returns 403 Not Allowed. What is the defect?

choices.B: Server-side request forgery reaching an internal-only host

q: I own two test accounts. With account A's token, GET https://api.shop-lab.example/v1/orders/1002 returns 200 and the body contains account B's shipping address and email. Account A's own order is 1001. With no token the same request returns 401. Which class?

choices.B: Missing authentication on a public route

q: Request with header Origin: https://attacker-lab.example to GET https://api.shop-lab.example/v1/me (session cookie attached) returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://attacker-lab.example and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true with the user's profile JSON. Which class?

An unauthenticated POST {"query":"{__schema{types{name fields{name}}}}"} to https://api.shop-lab.example/graphql returns the full schema, including mutations adminDeleteUser and setUserRole. No query returned any user data. Which description is most accurate?

choices.B: GraphQL introspection leak: a lead that maps privileged mutations to test for missing authorization

q: A sweep flagged https://portal.shop-lab.example/actuator . The response is 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="actuator" and an empty body. Which is correct?

choices.B: Protected endpoint: not a finding on its own, a lead at most

q: Confirmed: an unauthenticated GET proxy parameter fetches internal-only hosts and returns their bodies. Rules: GET only, no payloads that execute code. What is the best next escalation step?

choices.A: Send a POST with a shell command to the internal host
choices.B: Through the same proxy, GET credential-bearing internal paths such as /actuator/env or cloud metadata on the reachable internal hosts
choices.C: Port-scan all 65535 ports on every internal host
choices.D: Stop and file it as is

q: GET /actuator/env on an in-scope host returns 200 but every secret value is masked as "******". GET only. Which next request is most likely to recover a real credential?

choices.A: GET /actuator/heapdump (if registered) and search the dump for the property values

q: Which control best proves that a 200 on an unusual API path is a real route and not an SPA or catch-all response?

choices.A: Re-send the same request three times
choices.B: Compare against a nonsense sibling path on the same host: status, content-type, length and body must differ

q: An endpoint returns private JSON with no Authorization header. Which pair of requests best proves the response does not depend on any credential?

choices.A: No Authorization header and a fabricated Bearer token, both returning the same private body
choices.B: Two requests with a real token
choices.C: One request over HTTP/2 and one over HTTP/1.1

q: GET https://api.shop-lab.example/v2/api-docs returns a public OpenAPI JSON listing 140 routes. No route was called yet and no user data is in the response. What is it?

choices.B: A lead: use the route list to test which routes answer without authentication
choices.C: A false positive with no value

q: GET https://www.hotel-lab.example/actuator returns 403 from the edge. GET https://www.hotel-lab.example/%61ctuator returns 200 with the actuator links JSON. What is the defect?

choices.A: Access-control bypass: the edge rule matches the literal path but the origin decodes the percent-encoded one

q: Through an SSRF I captured an internal service's /actuator/threaddump: thread names, class names, internal hostnames and a zookeeper connect string, but no password, token or user record. How should it be classified?

choices.B: Internal reach with internal information disclosure: escalate toward a credential-bearing endpoint before filing

q: GET https://login.shop-lab.example/logout?next=https://attacker-lab.example returns 302 with Location: https://attacker-lab.example and no server-side fetch happens. Which class?
GET /api/user/1, /api/user/999999 and /api/user/abc on an in-scope host all return 200 with the identical 1234-byte body {"ok":true,"data":null}. Is this an IDOR?

choices.A: Yes, IDOR on every user id
choices.B: No: a catch-all response that ignores the id, a false positive
